name: RDF (Resource Description Framework)
summary: W3C graph data model in which statements are subject-predicate-object triples over IRIs, literals and blank nodes, grouped into graphs and datasets, with a model-theoretic semantics and several concrete syntaxes (RDF/XML, N-Triples, N-Quads, Turtle, TriG, JSON-LD). RDF 1.2 adds triple terms (reification, ex-RDF-star) and directional language-tagged strings.
standards: W3C RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax (2014)

level_notes.1: W3C Recommendations: RDF 1.1 (2014) Concepts, Semantics, RDF/XML, N-Triples, N-Quads are the current Recommendations; the RDF 1.2 suite (Concepts, Semantics, N-Triples, N-Quads, RDF/XML, Turtle, TriG) is in Candidate Recommendation and is linked alongside. RDF 1.0 (1999/2004) documents are linked for history. Turtle/TriG/N3 and RDF Schema have their own catalog entries (turtle, rdfs).
level_notes.0: The W3C rdf-tests repository holds the official test manifests for every syntax and for entailment. Major independent implementations: Apache Jena (Java), Eclipse RDF4J (Java), rdflib (Python), N3.js (JavaScript), Oxigraph (Rust), Raptor and Serd (C).
level_notes.2: The W3C RDF Primer (1.1 Note and 1.2 draft) is the official tutorial.
